note: The session's web-search allowance was used up before this part began, so it went by fetching official pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: county sites, school board pages, the Revenue Cabinet's PVA directory and the State Board of Elections' 2022 general election county recaps (elect.ky.gov). Many county recaps are image-only PDFs with no text layer (Anderson, Bourbon, Carter, Fleming, Grant, Greenup, Lee, Marshall, Metcalfe, Pendleton, Robertson, Spencer), and several county or city sites did not resolve (Lyon, Fleming, Bullitt, Lyndon, Newport Independent Schools' board page), so 18 of the 30 candidates are left blank. For contested 2022 races the recaps print precinct pages only; the outcome noted here (Hartlage, Guffey, Hardy, Blankenship) is the sum of the Total column across those pages and is confirmed by the official page that lists the person in the office today. Several candidates found here hold the office they seek today (Milam, Burton, Grimes, Hartlage, Pratt, Letcher, Hardy, Blankenship) while our record's incumbent flag is 0 for them; the county clerks' filing lists do not mark local incumbents, so this is noted rather than filed as a review item. Spencer County: the Revenue Cabinet's PVA directory names a Pam McClain only as an office contact, not as PVA, so nothing is recorded for Pamela McClain. Not holders today, by the official pages read: Sarah Froelich (Kenton District 1 is Beth Sewell), E. Spencer Keck (Hardin District 3 is Patsy Whitehead), Joshua D. Kight (Woodford District 8 is Jackie Brown), Remi Capps (Lee's Judge/Executive is Steve Mays Jr.), Jeff Aulick (Pendleton District 4 is Rick Mineer), Kenny Brockman (Robertson's sheriff is Randy Insko), LaKeysha Singleton (the 50th District's judge for Boyle County is Patrick Barsotti), Courtney Hundley (not on Erlanger's council page), Antonio Brown (not on St. Matthews' council page).
verifier_note: Every url re-opened on 2026-10-03 with the kit's User-Agent (states/net.py); recap PDFs read with ballot/pdftext.py. Removed: Sarah Froelich's endorsed_by (the Kenton County Democratic Party's page is headed '2026 Democratic Candidates' and never says it endorses: a candidates list, not an endorsement). Corrected: Froelich's website 'how' (the site's own title and footer now carry it) and her office source (the recap shows her among Park Hills council candidates; 'with the most votes' was not confirmed and is dropped). Peyton Griffee: House District 26 is on Bullitt County's ballot (State Board of Elections' 2022 Bullitt recap lists the 26th Representative District), so the site's Bullitt County and State Representative are the two anchors.
